s: A solutions architect is designing a solution to automatically provision new AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The solutions architect has enabled AWS Control Tower for the organization. The solution must enable security controls and create resources such as billing alarms after creating new AWS accounts. The solution must be scalable. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: Create a new AWS account in the organization. Deploy a blueprint to the new AWS account. Define a blueprint that creates resources such as billing alarms. Configure AWS Control Tower to apply the blueprint after creating the new AWS account

Create a new AWS account in the organization. Establish trusted access to the account by using an AWS Cloud Formation template. Enroll the new AWS account into AWS Control Tower. Deploy a blueprint to the new AWS account by using AWS Control Tower to provision resources.

Use Account Factory to initiate the creation of a new AWS account by using AWS Service Catalog. Configure a lifecycle event in AWS Control Tower that invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to deploy an AWS CloudFormation template by using the AWS Control Tower Execution role.

Use Account Factory to initiate the creation of a new AWS account by using AWS Control Tower. Define a blueprint that creates resources such as billing alarms. Configure AWS Control Tower to apply the blueprint after creating the new AWS account.
x: Debated. Control Tower Account Factory Customization (since late 2022) applies a blueprint automatically when Account Factory creates the account, with no custom code; the lifecycle-event + Lambda pattern (C) was the answer before AFC existed.

w.y: AWS Control Tower Account Factory Customization (AFC) lets you attach a blueprint (a CloudFormation-based Service Catalog product) that Control Tower deploys automatically when Account Factory creates or enrolls an account. Controls come from the OU. This is native, scalable and needs no custom code, so it has the least overhead. Lifecycle events plus Lambda also work but mean custom code to maintain.

o.A: Creating accounts outside Account Factory means they must be enrolled separately, and Control Tower doesn't auto-apply blueprints to unmanaged accounts.
o.B: Manual trusted-access setup and enrollment steps add overhead; Account Factory does this natively.
o.C: Works (the classic pattern), but a custom Lambda function driven by lifecycle events is more code to build and maintain than AFC blueprints.
o.D: Account Factory with an AFC blueprint provisions the account and deploys resources such as billing alarms automatically, with no custom code.

s: Customize accounts with Account Factory Customization (AFC)
